source.text: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων;

records.literal_gloss: Then come to the Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes saying, \v 2 Because of what the disciples of you break the tradition of the elders?

en.L: Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem come to Jesus, saying, \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples break the tradition of the elders?
en.B: Then Pharisees and scribes arrived from Jerusalem and put a question to Jesus: \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples go against the tradition handed down by the elders?
en.R: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came from Jerusalem to see Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 2 "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers break the rules that our leaders of long ago handed down?

fr.L: Alors des Pharisiens et des scribes venus de Jérusalem s’approchent de Jésus, disant : \v 2 « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples transgressent-ils la tradition des anciens ?
fr.B: Alors des Pharisiens et des scribes arrivèrent de Jérusalem et posèrent une question à Jésus : \v 2 « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples vont-ils contre la tradition transmise par les anciens ?
fr.R: Alors des Pharisiens et des spécialistes de la Loi sont venus de Jérusalem pour voir Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : \v 2 « Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples désobéissent aux règles que nos maîtres d’autrefois nous ont transmises ?

decisions.choice: the tradition of the elders: teaching handed down by earlier teachers alongside the written law
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept rules passed on from teacher to student that applied the law to daily life. Mark 7:3-4 describes some of them. They were not part of the written law.

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem: from the center of Jewish leadership
decisions.reason: These questioners have come a long way from the city of the temple and the high council. Their coming shows that Jesus's work is now watched from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: break: step over, fail to keep
decisions.reason: The verb means to go beyond a line. The same verb is used in Jesus's reply (15:3).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: go against (B), break (R), the same word at 15:2 and 15:3
alternatives: different words in the two verses
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with the verb of their own question. Each level keeps one word for both verses so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law; our leaders of long ago
decisions.reason: Readable says who the scribes were and that the elders here are teachers of earlier generations, not the town elders of the day.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("s’approchent", 15:12 "disent")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. Literal keeps the present where Matthew tells a past event in the present, as English Literal does.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens; les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for the Gospels, as in Mark 7:1; Readable follows the English "teachers of the law".

decisions.choice: les disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; French "disciple" is a common, transparent word, and the style guide keeps "les disciples" at every level, as in Mark's French. This holds for the whole passage.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not for they wash the hands of them when bread they eat.

en.L: For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
en.B: They eat their meals without first washing their hands."
en.R: They do not wash their hands in the special way before they eat."

fr.L: Car ils ne se lavent pas les mains quand ils mangent du pain. »
fr.B: Ils prennent leurs repas sans s’être d’abord lavé les mains. »
fr.R: Ils ne se lavent pas les mains selon le rite avant de manger. »

decisions.choice: wash their hands: a washing for religious purity, not for cleanliness
decisions.reason: The law required priests to wash their hands before serving (Exodus 30:19-21). The tradition extended a ritual washing to ordinary meals (Mark 7:3). Not doing it was a matter of purity, not hygiene.

decisions.choice: eat bread: eat a meal
decisions.reason: To eat bread is a common way of saying to have a meal.

decisions.choice: in the special way
decisions.reason: Readable shows that a ritual washing is meant, not ordinary washing.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said to them, Because of what also you break the commandment of the God because of the tradition of you?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Why do you also break the commandment of God because of your tradition?
en.B: He answered them, "And why do you go against God's commandment for the sake of your tradition?
en.R: Jesus answered, "And why do you break God's command so that you can keep your own rules?

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et leur dit : « Et vous, pourquoi transgressez-vous le commandement de Dieu à cause de votre tradition ?
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Et vous, pourquoi allez-vous contre le commandement de Dieu au nom de votre tradition ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Et vous, pourquoi désobéissez-vous au commandement de Dieu pour pouvoir garder vos propres règles ?

decisions.choice: you also: Jesus turns their charge back on them
alternatives: you as well as my disciples
decisions.reason: They accused the disciples of breaking a tradition. Jesus asks why they themselves break a command of God, which is far more serious.

decisions.choice: your tradition: rules of human making, set against God's command
decisions.reason: In 15:2 it was "the tradition of the elders". Jesus now calls it "your tradition", their own, in contrast with what God commanded.

decisions.choice: Jesus answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:9
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 3-9 are one answer, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

decisions.choice: transgresser (L), aller contre (B), désobéir à (R), the same verb at 15:2 and 15:3
decisions.reason: As in English, Jesus answers with the verb of their own question, so each level keeps one verb for both verses and the echo is heard.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·

records.literal_gloss: The for God said, Honor the father and the mother, and, The [one] speaking evil of father or mother in death let him end;

en.L: For God said, 'Honor [your] father and [your] mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'
en.B: For God said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and also, 'Anyone who reviles father or mother must be put to death.'
en.R: God said, 'Honor your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who says evil things against their father or mother must be put to death.'

fr.L: Car Dieu a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et : “Celui qui dit du mal de père ou de mère, qu’il soit mis à mort.”
fr.B: Dieu a dit en effet : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et aussi : “Celui qui insulte son père ou sa mère doit être mis à mort.”
fr.R: Dieu a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère.” Il a dit aussi : “Celui qui dit du mal de son père ou de sa mère doit être puni de mort.”

decisions.choice: honor your father and your mother: Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16
decisions.reason: The fifth commandment. Jesus calls it what God said, not only what Moses said.

decisions.choice: whoever speaks evil of father or mother: Exodus 21:17; Leviticus 20:9
decisions.reason: The law treated cursing a parent as a crime deserving death. "Let him end in death" copies a Hebrew way of speaking that stresses certainty.

decisions.choice: honor: respect, and also support and care for parents in old age
decisions.reason: Honoring parents included providing for them. This is the point of the example in 15:5-6.

decisions.choice: God said, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: God commanded, saying, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "God commanded, saying". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: reviles
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak evil of someone, to abuse with words.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς, οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: You but say, Whoever shall say to the father or the mother, A gift whatever by me you might be profited, \v 6 not not he shall honor the father of him; and you made void the word of the God because of the tradition of you.

en.L: But you say, 'Whoever says to father or mother, "Whatever help you might have had from me [is] a gift [to God]," \v 6 {{gender:that person|he}} shall certainly not honor {{gender:their|his}} father.' And you have made void the word of God because of your tradition.
en.B: But you teach that if someone says to father or mother, 'Any support you could have received from me is set apart as a gift to God,' \v 6 then that person is excused from honoring {{gender:their|his}} father. So for the sake of your tradition you have cancelled God's word.
en.R: But you teach something else. You say people can tell their father or mother, 'I cannot help you. What I would have given you is now a gift for God.' \v 6 Then they do not have to honor their father anymore. So you make God's word mean nothing, just to keep your own rules.

fr.L: Mais vous, vous dites : si quelqu’un dit à son père ou à sa mère : “Ce dont tu aurais pu profiter de ma part [est] une offrande [à Dieu]”, \v 6 il n’honorera certainement pas son père. Et vous avez annulé la parole de Dieu à cause de votre tradition.
fr.B: Mais vous, vous enseignez que si quelqu’un dit à son père ou à sa mère : “L’aide que tu aurais pu recevoir de moi est mise à part comme offrande à Dieu”, \v 6 celui-là est dispensé d’honorer son père. Ainsi, au nom de votre tradition, vous avez aboli la parole de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais vous, vous enseignez autre chose. Vous dites qu’on peut dire à son père ou à sa mère : “Je ne peux pas t’aider. Ce que je t’aurais donné est maintenant une offrande pour Dieu.” \v 6 Après cela, on n’a plus besoin d’honorer son père. Ainsi, vous faites comme si la parole de Dieu ne comptait pas, seulement pour garder vos propres règles.

decisions.choice: a gift: property vowed to God, so that it could not be used for the parents
decisions.reason: Mark 7:11 gives the Hebrew word for such an offering, Corban. Vows to God were binding (Numbers 30:2). A son could declare his goods vowed to God and so put them beyond his parents' reach, while he may still have kept the use of them himself.

decisions.choice: shall not honor his father: the result of their ruling, that such a person is freed from the duty
alternatives: Jesus's own comment: such a person will certainly not honor his father
decisions.reason: The words can be the last part of the teaching Jesus reports, saying the vow releases the son from supporting his father. They can also be Jesus's comment on what follows from it. Either way, the vow ends the son's care for his parents.

decisions.choice: the word of God, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the commandment of God, the reading of many later manuscripts
the law of God, in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "the word", others "the law", and many later ones "the commandment". All three point to the command of 15:4. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his father, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: his father or his mother, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "or his mother", to match 15:4 and 15:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|he}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The rule applies to a daughter as well as a son, so the inclusive forms are the default.

decisions.choice: I cannot help you; anymore
alternatives: a gift; he shall not honor
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vow meant for the parents.

decisions.choice: cancelled (B); make mean nothing (R)
decisions.reason: The verb was used for annulling a law or a contract.

decisions.choice: one level of quotation marks inside Jesus's words at Literal (“…”), with the rule they teach given as indirect speech
alternatives: a third level of quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:11: French marks a quotation within a quotation with “ ”, and a third level is awkward in French type. Literal reports the rule as Jesus's own statement ("vous dites : si quelqu’un dit…") and keeps the vow itself in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "quelqu’un … il" (L), "celui-là" (B), "son père"
decisions.reason: English needs a setting for "that person / he" and "their / his". French "quelqu’un", "il" and "celui-là" are the ordinary generic forms and already mean a son or a daughter, and the possessive "son" agrees with "père", not with the child, so, as the style guide says, no span is added.

source.text: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·

records.literal_gloss: Hypocrites, rightly prophesied concerning you Isaiah saying,

en.L: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied rightly about you, saying,
en.B: You are hypocrites, and Isaiah's prophecy about you was exactly right. He said:
en.R: You hypocrites! Long ago Isaiah spoke God's message, and he described you exactly. He said,

fr.L: Hypocrites ! Ésaïe a bien prophétisé à votre sujet, en disant :
fr.B: Vous êtes des hypocrites, et Ésaïe a vu juste quand il a prophétisé à votre sujet. Il a dit :
fr.R: Hypocrites ! Il y a très longtemps, Ésaïe a transmis le message de Dieu, et il vous a décrits exactement. Il a dit :

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people whose religion is a performance
decisions.reason: As in 6:2. Their outward care for purity hides a heart far from God (15:8).

decisions.choice: prophesied about you: Isaiah's words to his own generation fit these leaders too
alternatives: Isaiah spoke only of people in Jesus's day
decisions.reason: Isaiah spoke to the people of Jerusalem in his own time. Jesus says the words describe his hearers just as well.

decisions.choice: spoke God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is.

source.text: Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: The people this with the lips me honors, the but heart of them far away is from me;

en.L: 'This people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with [their] lips, but their heart is far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: 'With their lips this people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but their heart keeps far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: 'These people honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their words, but their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore des lèvres, mais leur cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: “Avec ses lèvres, ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore, mais son cœur reste éloigné de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: “Ces gens {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorent par leurs paroles, mais leur cœur est loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:13: God speaks of his people
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes in a form close to the Greek Old Testament. In Isaiah the Lord is the speaker, so "me" is God.

decisions.choice: this people honors me with their lips, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: this people draws near to me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "draws near to me with their mouth and", which is in the Greek of Isaiah 29:13. Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: As in 12:34. Honor in words means nothing when the heart, the person's real self, stays away from God.

decisions.choice: spans on "me" for God
decisions.reason: God speaks in Isaiah, so the pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as in 12:18.

decisions.choice: with their words
decisions.reason: Readable says what honoring with the lips means.

source.text: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: In vain but they worship me, teaching [as] teachings commandments of men.

en.L: and in vain they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, teaching [as] teachings [the] commandments of {{gender:people|men}}.'"
en.B: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is empty, for the doctrines they teach are commands made by human beings.'"
en.R: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} means nothing. They teach rules that people made up, as if those rules came from God.'"

fr.L: et c’est en vain qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent un culte, enseignant comme doctrines des commandements {{gender:d’humains|d’hommes}}.” »
fr.B: Le culte qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent est vide, car les doctrines qu’ils enseignent sont des commandements humains.” »
fr.R: Le culte qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent ne vaut rien. Ils enseignent des règles inventées par les gens, comme si elles venaient de Dieu.” »

decisions.choice: in vain: to no purpose, empty
decisions.reason: Their worship achieves nothing, because God does not accept it.

decisions.choice: teaching as doctrines the commands of people: presenting human rules as God's teaching
alternatives: teaching both God's law and human rules
decisions.reason: The fault is that rules made by people are taught as if they had God's authority. That is what Jesus has shown in 15:3-6.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: as if those rules came from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "teaching as doctrines" means here.

source.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε·

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] the crowd he said to them, Hear and understand;

en.L: And calling the crowd to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Listen and understand:
en.B: Then Jesus called the crowd over to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Hear this, and understand it.
en.R: Then Jesus called the crowd to come near. He said, "Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and understand what I say.

fr.L: Et ayant appelé la foule à [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Écoutez et comprenez :
fr.B: Puis Jésus appela la foule auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et dit : « Écoutez, et comprenez bien.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a appelé la foule à s’approcher. Il a dit : « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et comprenez ce que je dis.

decisions.choice: calling the crowd: the teaching is for everyone, not only the leaders
alternatives: a private word to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from the Pharisees and scribes to the whole crowd. What makes a person unclean concerns everyone.

decisions.choice: understand: grasp the meaning, not only hear the words
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the parables of chapter 13 (13:13-15, 19, 23). Hearing is not enough without understanding.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new part of the scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:11
alternatives: closing the quotation in this sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 10-11 are one saying.

source.text: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: Not the entering into the mouth defiles the man, but the going out of the mouth this defiles the man.

en.L: It is not what enters into the mouth [that] defiles the {{gender:person|man}}, but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles the {{gender:person|man}}."
en.B: A person is not made unclean by what goes into the mouth. What makes a person unclean is what comes out of it."
en.R: What you put into your mouth does not make you unclean before God. It is what comes out of your mouth that makes you unclean."

fr.L: Ce n’est pas ce qui entre dans la bouche qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}, mais ce qui sort de la bouche, voilà ce qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}. »
fr.B: Ce n’est pas ce qui entre dans la bouche qui rend une personne impure. Ce qui la rend impure, c’est ce qui en sort. »
fr.R: Ce que vous mettez dans votre bouche ne vous rend pas impurs devant Dieu. Ce qui vous rend impurs, c’est ce qui sort de votre bouche. »

decisions.choice: defiles: makes a person unclean, unfit to come before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common or impure. Purity decided whether a person could take part in worship (Leviticus 11-15).

decisions.choice: what comes out of the mouth: words, and the heart they come from
decisions.reason: Jesus explains in 15:18-19 that what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart.

decisions.choice: the saying answers the question of washed hands (15:20)
alternatives: a ruling that sets aside all the food laws
decisions.reason: Matthew applies the saying to eating with unwashed hands (15:20) and does not include Mark's comment that Jesus made all foods clean (Mark 7:19). How far the saying bears on the food laws themselves is debated.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the inclusive form is the default. The same applies in 15:18 and 15:20.

decisions.choice: before God
decisions.reason: Readable says in whose sight a person is unclean.

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} at Literal; "une personne" (B), "vous" (R) with no setting
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:15: the setting goes on the noun French has to choose. "L’être humain" and "l’homme" are both masculine, so the words that refer back to them are the same under either option; Balanced and Readable are already inclusive. The same holds in 15:18 and 15:20.

source.text: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν;

records.literal_gloss: Then having come the disciples say to him, Do you know that the Pharisees having heard the saying were offended?

en.L: Then the disciples come and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard the saying?"
en.B: Then the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} aware that the Pharisees took offense at what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said?"
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that the Pharisees were upset by what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said?"

fr.L: Alors les disciples s’approchent et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Sais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que les Pharisiens ont été scandalisés en entendant cette parole ? »
fr.B: Alors les disciples s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et dirent : « Sais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que les Pharisiens ont été choqués par ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit ? »
fr.R: Alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples sont venus vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais que les Pharisiens ont été fâchés par ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit ? »

decisions.choice: were offended: were shocked and angered, and so turned against him
decisions.reason: The verb pictures stumbling over something (11:6). The saying made them reject Jesus's teaching.

decisions.choice: the saying: the words of 15:11
decisions.reason: The disciples most likely mean the saying about what defiles. It struck at the purity rules the Pharisees kept with care.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: what you said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose saying it was.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said, Every plant which not planted the Father of me the heavenly will be uprooted.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "Every plant which {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
en.B: He answered, "Any plant that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven did not plant will be torn out, roots and all.
en.R: Jesus answered, "My Father in heaven will dig up every plant that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not plant.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et dit : « Toute plante que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père céleste n’a pas plantée sera déracinée.
fr.B: Il répondit : « Toute plante que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père du ciel n’a pas plantée sera arrachée avec ses racines.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Mon Père qui est au ciel va arracher toutes les plantes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas plantées.

decisions.choice: plant: the Pharisees and their teaching, which God did not plant
decisions.reason: Israel was pictured as God's planting (Isaiah 60:21; 61:3). Jesus says these leaders and their tradition do not come from God. Compare the weeds sown among the wheat (13:24-30).

decisions.choice: will be uprooted: God will uproot it, at the judgment
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the subject unsaid, but the Father who plants is the one who uproots. The next verse tells the disciples to leave them alone.

decisions.choice: My Father in heaven will dig up
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who acts, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:14
alternatives: closing the quotation in this sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 are one answer.

source.text: ἄφετε αὐτούς· τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοί τυφλῶν· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται.

records.literal_gloss: Leave them; blind they are guides of blind; blind and blind if guides, both into a pit will fall.

en.L: Leave them; they are blind guides of [the] blind. And if a blind [person] guides a blind [person], both will fall into a pit."
en.B: Pay no attention to them. They are blind, yet they guide others who are blind. When one blind person guides another, the two of them end up in a ditch."
en.R: Do not worry about them. They are like blind people leading other blind people. If a blind person leads another blind person, they will both fall into a hole."

fr.L: Laissez-les : ce sont des guides aveugles d’aveugles. Et si un aveugle guide un aveugle, tous deux tomberont dans une fosse. »
fr.B: Ne vous occupez pas d’eux. Ce sont des aveugles qui guident d’autres aveugles. Quand un aveugle en guide un autre, ils finissent tous les deux dans le fossé. »
fr.R: Ne vous inquiétez pas pour eux. Ils sont comme des aveugles qui conduisent d’autres aveugles. Si un aveugle conduit un autre aveugle, ils vont tomber tous les deux dans un trou. »

decisions.choice: leave them: let them be; do not be troubled about them
decisions.reason: The verb has a range of meanings. Here Jesus tells the disciples not to worry about the Pharisees' offense.

decisions.choice: blind guides: teachers who cannot see God's will and lead others astray
alternatives: people who are blind in body
decisions.reason: Teachers of the law saw themselves as guides of the blind (Romans 2:19). Jesus says they cannot see themselves (23:16, 24).

decisions.choice: blind guides of the blind, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: they are blind guides, in some early manuscripts
the same words in a different order, in others
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Some early ones lack "of the blind", and others order the words differently. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: ditch
decisions.reason: The word means a hole or ditch in the ground. Balanced uses the word most natural for a fall on a road.

source.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολήν ταύτην.

records.literal_gloss: Answering and the Peter said to him, Explain to us the parable this.

en.L: And Peter answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Explain this parable to us."
en.B: Peter spoke up: "Tell us what this parable means."
en.R: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Explain to us what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} meant by this saying."

fr.L: Et Pierre, prenant la parole, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Explique-nous cette parabole. »
fr.B: Pierre intervint : « Dis-nous ce que signifie cette parabole. »
fr.R: Pierre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Explique-nous ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as voulu dire par ces paroles. »

decisions.choice: parable: a saying in picture language, a riddle
decisions.reason: The word covers short sayings as well as stories. Peter means the saying of 15:11, and perhaps of 15:13-14 too.

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up in response to what had been said
decisions.reason: No question was asked. As often, the word introduces a reply to the situation. Peter speaks for the disciples (15:16 answers them all).

decisions.choice: this saying
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word, since there is no story here.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;

records.literal_gloss: He and said, Still also you without understanding are?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Are you also still without understanding?
en.B: He said, "Are even you still so slow to understand?
en.R: Jesus said, "Even now, do you still not understand, just like the others?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Vous aussi, êtes-vous encore sans intelligence ?
fr.B: Il dit : « Même vous, vous êtes encore si lents à comprendre ?
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Même maintenant, vous ne comprenez toujours pas, comme les autres ?

decisions.choice: you also: even the disciples, like the crowd and the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Jesus expected his disciples to understand what outsiders did not (13:11, 16).

decisions.choice: still: even now, after all they have heard
decisions.reason: The word stresses how long they have been with him.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 15:20
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 16-20 are one answer.

source.text: οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται;

records.literal_gloss: Not do you understand that everything entering into the mouth into the stomach goes and into a latrine is cast out?

en.L: Do you not understand that everything that enters into the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into [the] latrine?
en.B: Can you not see that everything taken in by the mouth goes down into the stomach and is then passed out into the latrine?
en.R: You know that the food you eat goes into your stomach and then passes out of your body.

fr.L: Ne comprenez-vous pas que tout ce qui entre dans la bouche va dans le ventre et est rejeté aux latrines ?
fr.B: Ne voyez-vous pas que tout ce qui entre par la bouche descend dans l’estomac, puis est évacué aux latrines ?
fr.R: Vous le savez bien : la nourriture que vous mangez va dans votre estomac, puis elle sort de votre corps.

decisions.choice: latrine: the place where waste is passed
decisions.reason: The word names a toilet or drain. Food passes through the body and is gone.

decisions.choice: do you not understand: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to see what is plain: food never reaches the heart.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question assumes.

source.text: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται, κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: The things but going out of the mouth out of the heart come out, and those defile the man.

en.L: But the things coming out of the mouth come out of the heart, and those defile the {{gender:person|man}}.
en.B: But what comes out of the mouth has its source in the heart, and that is what makes a person unclean.
en.R: But what comes out of your mouth comes from your heart. Those things make you unclean.

fr.L: Mais ce qui sort de la bouche vient du cœur, et c’est cela qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.B: Mais ce qui sort de la bouche prend sa source dans le cœur, et c’est cela qui rend une personne impure.
fr.R: Mais ce qui sort de votre bouche vient de votre cœur. Ce sont ces choses-là qui vous rendent impurs.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: As in 15:8. What a person says and does comes from what is within (12:34).

decisions.choice: uncleanness begins inside a person
alternatives: uncleanness is only a matter of the body
decisions.reason: Jesus moves the question from the hands and the stomach to the heart.

source.text: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί, φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, ψευδομαρτυρίαι, βλασφημίαι.

records.literal_gloss: Out of for the heart come out thoughts evil, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.

en.L: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.
en.B: It is from the heart that evil schemes come, and murder, adultery and other sexual sin, theft, false witness and abusive speech.
en.R: The heart is where evil thoughts come from. Murder, adultery, other sexual sins, stealing, lying in court, and saying hurtful things about others all come from there too.

fr.L: Car du cœur sortent les pensées mauvaises, meurtres, adultères, immoralités sexuelles, vols, faux témoignages, calomnies.
fr.B: C’est du cœur que viennent les mauvais desseins, le meurtre, l’adultère et les autres péchés sexuels, le vol, le faux témoignage et les paroles injurieuses.
fr.R: C’est du cœur que viennent les mauvaises pensées. Le meurtre, l’adultère, les autres péchés sexuels, le vol, le mensonge devant un tribunal, les paroles qui blessent les autres : tout cela vient aussi de là.

decisions.choice: murder, adultery, theft, false witness: the order of the sixth to ninth commandments
decisions.reason: The list follows Exodus 20:13-16. Jesus has spoken of the fifth commandment in 15:4.

decisions.choice: evil thoughts: wicked plans and reasonings
decisions.reason: The word means reasonings or plans. They are named first, as the root of the deeds that follow.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual sin of every kind
decisions.reason: The word is broad and covers sexual sin besides adultery.

decisions.choice: slanders: abusive speech against others, or against God
decisions.reason: The word can mean blasphemy against God or slander against people. Next to false witness, harm to others is in view, though both may be meant.

decisions.choice: evil schemes (B); lying in court (R); abusive speech (B), saying hurtful things about others (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe each wrong in plain words.

source.text: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον, τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: These are the things defiling the man, the but with unwashed hands to eat not defiles the man.

en.L: These are the things that defile the {{gender:person|man}}; but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile the {{gender:person|man}}."
en.B: These are what make a person unclean. Eating without washing one's hands does not make anyone unclean."
en.R: These are the things that make a person unclean. But if you eat without washing your hands in the special way, that does not make you unclean."

fr.L: Ce sont ces choses qui souillent {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} ; mais manger avec des mains non lavées ne souille pas {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}. »
fr.B: Voilà ce qui rend une personne impure. Manger sans s’être lavé les mains ne rend personne impur. »
fr.R: Ce sont ces choses-là qui rendent une personne impure. Mais si vous mangez sans vous être lavé les mains selon le rite, cela ne vous rend pas impurs. »

decisions.choice: eating with unwashed hands: the answer to the question of 15:2
decisions.reason: The chapter returns to where it began. The tradition of washing does not decide whether a person is clean before God.

decisions.choice: in the special way
decisions.reason: As in 15:2, Readable shows that a ritual washing is meant.
